correctness.rationale: The antipalindromic-closure recursion yields the stated closed words. For \(A_n\), one-letter factors force opposite parities and every factor of length at least two has an interval occurrence union; the only opposite-parity pair avoiding the critical \(10\) union is the endpoint pair, giving \(n^2-1\). For \(B_n\), length-two factors force two interior positions in opposite mod-4 residue classes. The length-four factor \(0011\) excludes exactly two endpoint-near pairs, while length-three residue checks and the central-interval property of every length-at-least-four factor prove all remaining candidates work. No singleton can cover both one-letter factors. Independent brute-force rechecks for \(3\le n\le6\) reproduced both classifications.

value.rationale: The number and geometry of all smallest attractors is a strictly finer invariant than minimum cardinality, and the two families are not arbitrary slices: they are the exceptional antipalindromic patterns singled out by the motivating theorem. The exact residue classifications and multiplicities therefore form a natural complete classification.

final_claim: For \(n\ge3\), every smallest string attractor is classified explicitly for the two exceptional antipalindromic pseudostandard families \(A_n=(01)^n\) and \(B_n=0(1100)^{n-1}1\), giving exactly \(n^2-1\) and \(2n(n-2)\) minimum attractors respectively.
limitations: Only the two stated directive families are classified.
